What CRISPR is

CRISPR (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats) is a gene-editing technology adapted from a natural bacterial immune system. 

In bacteria, it stores fragments of viral DNA and uses them with CRISPR-associated (Cas) proteins (most famously Cas9)

A team in Cuttack has shown that an AI-designed enzyme can edit rice DNA in several different ways. They also regenerated edited plants and grew them to maturity.
